symptom: `create agent … (UsageType: Conversational)`, the value the agents skill and the reference page taught, passed check, exec and docker check. At startup Agent Editor refused to import the agent ('UsageType_StringToEnum: No valid option for UsageType', then 'Usage Type is not valid for the Agent'), and in the reporter's app the published MCP server did not start either.
cause: UsageType is free-form in MDL and mxbuild does not read agent documents. AgentEditorCommons.UsageType_StringToENUM accepts only toLowerCase = 'task' (Single_Call) and 'chat' (Conversational), and AgentFromModel_Validate also refuses an empty one. The docs used the AgentCommons enumeration's caption, Conversational, instead of the string the import reads.
fix: MDL-AGENT05 warns, on create and on alter … set UsageType, for a value other than Task or Chat (any case), and for a create with none. The suggestion names Chat for Conversational and Task for Single_Call. The skill, reference page and error-message appendix now say Task | Chat.
insight: For an agent-editor string, the authority is the import microflow that reads it, not the enumeration it maps onto: describe AgentEditorCommons.UsageType_StringToENUM and AgentFromModel_Validate, after `mxcli marketplace install 257918`, to see the switch. Those two microflows also showed that an omitted value is refused, which the issue did not mention.
test: mdl/executor/validate_agent_usage_type_2309_test.go (Conversational, conversational, unset and alter set 'SingleCall' warn; Task, task and Chat do not). A pre-fix binary's check passed the issue's script silently.
